answer: I'd like to talk about a birthday that started badly and ended as one of my favourite days. A time I was pleasantly surprised was on my birthday a couple of years ago, when I was convinced everyone had forgotten. It was a working day, nobody at the office said a word, and even my family seemed unusually quiet at breakfast. The day had passed quietly, and honestly I felt a little [[dejected]], assuming no one had remembered. When I got home in the evening, tired and expecting a quiet dinner, my friends and family jumped out and surprised me with a party. I was completely [[taken aback]]; I genuinely had no idea they had been planning it. It turned out my younger sister had organised the whole thing and had sworn everyone to secrecy. My friends had apparently been hiding in my room for almost an hour. The whole thing was wonderfully [[thoughtful]], with my favourite food, decorations and even a homemade cake. What moved me most was realising how much effort they had gone to in secret. That moment turned a gloomy day into one of the happiest I can remember, and I felt a real lump in my throat. What surprised me most was how convincingly everyone had [[kept a straight face]] all day. Honestly, the surprise meant far more to me than any expensive gift could have. Even my grandparents called from the village later that night to wish me well. It was a powerful reminder of how [[fortunate]] I am to have such caring people in my life.

followUps.q: Do you like surprises in general?
followUps.answer: Pleasant ones, yes. I am not keen on surprises at work, like a sudden deadline, but a surprise like that party is wonderful, because it shows someone was thinking about you.

followUps.q: Have you ever organised a surprise for someone else?
followUps.answer: Yes, for my father when he retired. I gathered his old friends and relatives for a small celebration, and seeing his face was worth all the secret planning.

note: Persona fix: he lives with family, so 'empty flat' became a quiet dinner and the surprise was by friends and family, organised by his younger sister; added 'kept a straight face'.
